chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Sometimes I intend a matter and two inclinations arise in me, one commanding me and the other forbidding me.' He said, 'If you are in such a state, then pray two rak'ahs and seek God's guidance (istikhara) a hundred times and one time. Then see which of the two matters is more decisive for you and do it, for the good is in it, if God wills. And let your istikhara be in health/soundness, for perhaps a man is chosen for the cutting of his hand, the death of his child, and the loss of his wealth.'

key_terms.عَافِيَة: Health/soundness (from which the choice is made)
key_terms.قَطْعُ يَدٍ: Cutting of the hand (a specific hardship)

ai.seo_question: How to perform Istikhara prayer and seek guidance when undecided between two choices?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the method of Istikhara is specified as a two-rak'ah prayer followed by a hundred supplications, with the decision guided by the 'more decisive inclination' (ahzam al-amrayn). This highlights the Shia understanding that divine choice may involve hardship, as the Prophet and Imams note that the 'good' in a chosen path might be the removal of a calamity rather than immediate ease, emphasizing trust in Allah's wisdom over personal desire.
